Description: Specifies a max number of lines per function (set to 35).
Why This Rule is Included: Shorter functions are more readable.

Description: Specifies a max number of lines per file (set to 300).
Why This Rule is Included: Shorter files are more navigable.

Description: Specifies a character limit on lines of code (set to 120).
Why This Rule is Included: Long lines are difficult to read.

Description: Disallow deeply nested callbacks (set to 3).
Why This Rule is Included: Deeply nested callbacks are difficult to reason about.

Description: Disallows declaring variables that are not used.
Why This Rule is Included: Values that are not used should not be a part of production code.

Description: Disallows usage of console logging.
Why This Rule is Included: Logging or debugging code should not be a part of production code.

Description: Enforce consistent naming formatting (set to camelCase).
Why This Rule is Included: Readability and consistency throughout the codebase.

Description: Functions must have a return type annotation.
Why This Rule is Included: Annotating return types improves readability of code.

Description: Disallows usage of "magic" numbers.
Why This Rule is Included: Magic numbers result in code that is difficult to generalize and extend.

Description: Require usage of `public`, `private`, and `protected` for method declarations.
Why This Rule is Included: Annotating improves readability and encourages developers to consider appropriate usage.

Description: Specifies a way write type annotations for generic types (i.e. Set, Array).
Why This Rule is Included: Though there are several ways to do this, we choose one for consistency.

Description: Use the `?` operator to access potentially null attributes when possible.
Why This Rule is Included: This is the best practice for javascript code, and results in concise code.

Description: Use `for...of` when iterating.
Why This Rule is Included: Best practice in javascript. Many loops are simple and do not require explicit variable iterator declarations.

Description: Use `const` if possible.
Why This Rule is Included: This is the best practice for javascript code. Using `const` communicates the value does not change.

Description: Disallow usage of `var`.
Why This Rule is Included: Use `let` or `const` instead.

Description: Use foo.bar instead of foo["bar"] when accessing object attributes
Why This Rule is Included: This is the best practice for javascript code.

Description: Variables in methods may not share (shadow) names of the class's attributes.
Why This Rule is Included: Shadowed variables may cause confusion and result in mistaken references.

Description: Use `===` instead of `==`.
Why This Rule is Included: Using `==` results in unexpected behavior in javascript.

Description: Enforces that promises be `await`ed or otherwise handled.
Why This Rule is Included: Usage of promises is error prone. Floating promises are a common issue.

Description: `await` may not be used in a loop.
Why This Rule is Included: For performance reasons, use `Promise.all(...)` instead to take advantage of concurrency.

Description: Disallow `Promise(executorFunc()=>....).`
Why This Rule is Included: Use the `resolve, reject` promise API.

Description: Disallow `await`ing something that is not a `Promise`.
Why This Rule is Included: Awaiting something that is not a promise does not flag an error, but gives the reader a false impression of the value.

Description: Flag usages of promises that imply the user is expecting to use the value of the promise but has not yet `await`ed it yet.
Why This Rule is Included: Using promisies is error prone. A developer can easily forget to await a promise.

Description: Enforces that functions that use promises are marked as `async`.
Why This Rule is Included: Since promises are naturally asynchronous, their invoking function should also be annotated as such.
